To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we proposed a new constrained formulation that combines a knowledge transfer and a regression functions with additional constraints to learn visual classifiers from text descriptions, and we showed that the proposed constrained model is superior over several baselines.

1) we can predict a visual classifier from unstructured text, 2) the prediction is better if the text is more descriptive and informative, 3) the prediction is also better if the text has more visual concepts and is less ambiguous, and 4) the prediction is more accurate when we use a distributional semantics based kernel function in the text space.
(i) we can learn visual classifiers from text, (ii) we can learn a kernelized model to predict visual classifiers from text and (iii) we can learn text kernels for predicting visual classifiers.

a challenging problem that has not been studied before.
the question of how to utilize textual descriptions to learn visual classifiers, and our results indicate that it is possible to successfully predict visual classifiers from unstructured text.
the problem of learning visual classifiers from purely textual descriptions, and we have developed several novel models and techniques to solve this problem.

we can learn visual classifiers from text descriptions of visual classes with a high level of accuracy, which could be useful in many applications.
our model is able to successfully learn the parameters of a classifier from unstructured text description of classes.

we can predict classifiers for visual categories from purely textual descriptions with reasonable accuracies, which is a novel result and an important step toward the vision of learning visual classifiers from natural language descriptions.

we propose and evaluate a novel approach to learn visual classifiers from unstructured text descriptions, which could be a step forward in the direction of utilizing text in visual recognition tasks.
we proposed a novel problem and studied it from different perspectives.
we proposed several formulations that learn visual classifiers from purely unstructured text descriptions of visual categories, which could potentially have a significant impact in many applications.

the visual classifiers could be successfully predicted from unstructured text descriptions of visual classes with high accuracy.
